title: Marked relative-nerve adjunction and its comparison with unstraightening
statement:
Use marked simplicial sets and the absolute marked model category $\mathsf M$ of [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model], the relative cocartesian model category of [lem-coef-marked-relative-cartesian-model] (the opposite of its cartesian version), and the projective diagram conventions of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-coherent-diagrams]. Fix sufficiently large nested universes and a small ordinary category $C$. For a strict functor $F:C\to\mathsf M$, let $U(c)$ be its underlying simplicial set. Define $N_C^+(F)$ over $N(C)$ as follows. An $n$-simplex is a string $\sigma:[n]\to C$ and maps $t_J:\Delta^J\to U(\sigma(\max J))$, for all nonempty $J\subseteq[n]$, with
$$t_J|_{\Delta^I}=U(\sigma(\max I)\to\sigma(\max J))t_I\qquad(\varnothing\ne I\subseteq J).$$
For $\theta:[m]\to[n]$ the new components are $t'_J=t_{\theta(J)}\Delta(\theta|_J)$. An edge over $c\to d$ is marked precisely when its component $t_{\{0,1\}}$ is marked in $F(d)$.

The functor $N_C^+:\mathsf M^C\to\mathsf M_{N(C)}^{\mathrm{cocart}}$ has a left adjoint and the adjunction is a Quillen equivalence for the projective model structure on $\mathsf M^C$. Here projective weak equivalences and fibrations are objectwise, and a Quillen equivalence means a Quillen adjunction inducing mutually inverse derived functors on the localized homotopy theories. In particular $N_C^+$ sends projectively fibrant diagrams to fibrant objects, with exactly the displayed marking.

On projectively fibrant diagrams there is a natural weak-equivalence comparison of $N_C^+$ with cocartesian unstraightening, using the ordinary coherent-nerve diagram of $F$ in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$. Unstraightening is the inverse of the equivalence in [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening], or its marked model from [lem-coef-marked-cone-straightening-quillen]. Under the canonical equivalences identifying the fibre of derived unstraightening at $c$ with the quasicategory underlying $F(c)$, this comparison identifies its fibre functor with the identity up to coherent natural equivalence. This is a comparison of derived functors, retaining their mapping spaces and higher coherence, natural in strict transformations of $F$. For a functor $u:C'\to C$, the formula gives a canonical marked isomorphism $N_{C'}^+(Fu)\cong N(u)^*N_C^+(F)$; the derived comparison respects these isomorphisms coherently for identities and composites.

source.place: HTT Definition 3.2.5.12, Remark 3.2.5.14, Proposition 3.2.5.18(2), and Corollary 3.2.5.20, with the comparison of Remark 3.2.5.16 and Lemma 3.2.5.17; cocartesian variance. Read online. WANTED: local archive of HTT. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: The models and their lifting classes are [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model] and the cocartesian opposite in [lem-coef-marked-relative-cartesian-model]. Regard the ordinary small $C$ as a simplicial category with discrete hom sets. [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus] gives the projective model structure on $\mathsf M^C$ without any cofibrancy assumption on a diagram: weak equivalences and fibrations are objectwise. In the displayed relative-nerve formula, restricting first by $\theta$ and then by $\psi$ gives the same components as restricting by $\theta\psi$: images of subsets compose and $\max\theta(J)=\theta(\max J)$. The compatibility equation therefore survives restriction. Postcomposition by a strict transformation gives a functor on diagrams. A degenerate edge has degenerate last-fibre component and is marked, so the edge test defines a marked simplicial set. It also shows that transformations preserve markings.

Construct the left adjoint explicitly. For $p:X\to N(C)$ set $L_C(X)(c)_r=\{(x,g):x\in X_r,\ g:p(x_r)\to c\}$, with $\theta^*(x,g)=(\theta^*x,g\,p(x_{\theta(s)}\to x_r))$ for $\theta:[s]\to[r]$; mark $(e,g)$ just when $e$ is marked in $X$. Postcomposition of $g$ gives the diagram maps; associativity in $C$ checks every simplicial and diagram identity. Given a marked map $b:X\to N_C^+(F)$, let $t^x_J$ be the components of $b(x)$ and define $h_c(x,g)=F(g)(t^x_{[r]})$ as an $r$-simplex of $F(c)$. The restriction equation for $t^x$ gives $\theta^*h_c(x,g)=h_c(\theta^*x,g\,p(x_{\theta(s)}\to x_r))$, and marked edges remain marked. Conversely, from a strict transformation $h:L_C(X)\to F$ define $t^x_J$ by applying $h_{p(x_{\max J})}$ to $(x|_J,\mathrm{id})$, including all the faces of this simplex. Naturality in $c$ gives exactly the displayed subset compatibility equation, and simplicial naturality gives the operators. These assignments are inverse: the recovery of $h_c(x,g)$ uses its naturality for $g$, while the recovery of $t^x_J$ uses restriction to $J$. They commute with precomposition in $X$ and postcomposition in $F$, giving $L_C\dashv N_C^+$. All sets used have the chosen small size. This is a direct construction, not an appeal to an uncited adjoint-functor theorem.

source.place: Remark 3.2.5.13, with its left adjoint constructed explicitly from Definition 3.2.5.2

proof.text: Show that $L_C$ preserves cofibrations by its adjunction. Let $F\to G$ be an objectwise trivial fibration. From the weak factorization systems in [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model], its components lift against every marked monomorphism, hence against $(\partial\Delta^n)^\flat\to(\Delta^n)^\flat$, and they reflect markings by lifting against $(\Delta^1)^\flat\to(\Delta^1)^\sharp$. In a boundary lifting problem for $N_C^+(F)\to N_C^+(G)$ over a string $\sigma:[n]\to C$, the components $t_J$ for proper nonempty $J\subsetneq[n]$ are fixed by the boundary. Push them to $F(\sigma(n))$ along $\sigma(\max J)\to\sigma(n)$; the subset equations make them the faces of a map $\partial\Delta^n\to F(\sigma(n))$. Lift the full component against $F(\sigma(n))\to G(\sigma(n))$. This also works for $n=0$, when the boundary is empty. The resulting full component supplies the required simplex and all its equations. If an edge downstairs is marked, reflection of markings in the last-fibre component makes its lifted edge marked. For any marked monomorphism, apply [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells] to its underlying monomorphism. At each dimension its coproduct of boundary attachments admits lifts by the preceding argument; the pushout property glues these with the previously chosen lift, and their sequential colimit gives a simplicial lift on the entire target; then reflection of markings ensures the map respects every marked edge of the target of the monomorphism. Thus $N_C^+$ preserves trivial fibrations in the cocartesian relative model of [lem-coef-marked-relative-cartesian-model]. Adjunction transfers each diagonal lifting problem, so $L_C$ sends every cofibration to a projective cofibration.

Put $T_C(X)=(\operatorname{St}^+_{\epsilon_C}(X^{\mathrm{op}}))^{\mathrm{op}}$ as in [lem-cbc-relative-nerve-cone-left-comparison]. The opposite models of [lem-coef-marked-relative-cartesian-model] and the cone theorem [lem-coef-marked-cone-straightening-quillen] show that $T_C$ is left Quillen. Here the valuewise opposite is an automorphism of $\mathsf M^C$ preserving the projective structure: opposite preserves monomorphisms and markings, $(K^{\mathrm{op}})^
atural=(K^
atural)^{\mathrm{op}}$ for a quasicategory $K$, and $\operatorname{Map}^\sharp(Y^{\mathrm{op}},K^
atural)\cong\operatorname{Map}^\sharp(Y,(K^{\mathrm{op}})^
atural)^{\mathrm{op}}$ through $(\Delta^n)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\Delta^n$, so by the weak-equivalence test of [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model] it preserves and reflects weak equivalences (a simplicial set and its opposite have homeomorphic realizations). Every relative object is cofibrant, so [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] shows that $T_C$ preserves every weak equivalence. The new comparison node gives an objectwise weak equivalence $a_X:T_C(X)	o L_C(X)$ for every $X$, with exactly the $L_C$ constructed in step 2. For a weak equivalence $f:X	o Y$, naturality says $L_C(f)a_X=a_YT_C(f)$. Two-out-of-three in the projective model now makes $L_C(f)$ an objectwise weak equivalence. Together with step 3 this proves that $L_C$ preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations. Thus its adjunction with $N_C^+$ is Quillen; no assumption that $X$ is fibrant or that $F$ is projectively cofibrant has entered.

source.place: Lemma 3.2.5.17(2) and first paragraph of the proof of Proposition 3.2.5.18(2)

proof.text: The counit $\epsilon_C:\mathfrak C[N(C)^{\mathrm{op}}]\to C^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence by [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]: $C^{\mathrm{op}}$ is locally Kan (its hom spaces are discrete), its coherent nerve is the ordinary nerve, every simplicial set is Joyal-cofibrant, and $C^{\mathrm{op}}$ is Bergner-fibrant with cofibrant $N(C^{\mathrm{op}})$; since the derived coherent nerve is an equivalence, so is the derived $\mathfrak C$, and [lem-coef-quillen-derived-counit-criterion] makes this ordinary counit a weak equivalence. The unit and counit equivalences of [lem-coef-marked-cone-straightening-quillen], taking opposites, consequently make the derived adjunction of $T_C$ an equivalence. By [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], step 4 gives a derived adjunction $\mathbf L L_C\dashv\mathbf R N_C^+$. All source objects are cofibrant, and the transformation $a$ of [lem-cbc-relative-nerve-cone-left-comparison] is pointwise a weak equivalence, so it localizes to a coherent natural equivalence $\mathbf L T_C\simeq\mathbf L L_C$. Hence $\mathbf L L_C$ is an equivalence too. Step 6 identifies $\mathbf R N_C^+$ with the inverse cone right functor by an explicit mate, completing the asserted Quillen equivalence including its mapping spaces. In particular [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] gives preservation of fibrations by $N_C^+$, so a projectively fibrant $F$ goes to a fibrant relative object. Its marking is still its construction's exact last-fibre marking; the cocartesian model's fibrant-object characterization in [lem-coef-marked-relative-cartesian-model] identifies it with all cocartesian edges.

source.place: End of the proof of Proposition 3.2.5.18(2); Theorem 3.2.0.1; Proposition 3.1.4.1 in cocartesian variance

proof.text:
Write $V_C(F)=(\operatorname{Un}^+_{\epsilon_C}(F^{\mathrm{op}}))^{\mathrm{op}}$, the right adjoint of $T_C$. Take the right mate of $a:T_C\to L_C$: for projectively fibrant $F$ its component $\beta_F:N_C^+(F)\to V_C(F)$ is adjoint under $T_C\dashv V_C$ to
$$T_CN_C^+(F)\xrightarrow{a}L_CN_C^+(F)\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_F}F.$$
This is a natural marked map over $N(C)$. The ordinary counit $\varepsilon_F$ is a weak equivalence by [lem-coef-quillen-derived-counit-criterion]: step 5 gives the left derived equivalence and $N_C^+(F)$ is cofibrant in the relative marked model. Also $a$ is an objectwise weak equivalence by [lem-cbc-relative-nerve-cone-left-comparison]. At the level of the derived adjunctions of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], the displayed map equals the composite of $\mathbf L T_C(\beta_F)$ with the derived counit for $T_C\dashv V_C$, by the defining mate equation. Both this displayed map and that cone counit are equivalences. Two-out-of-three makes $\mathbf L T_C(\beta_F)$ an equivalence; applying the inverse cone functor makes $\beta_F$ an equivalence. Thus $\mathbf R N_C^+\simeq\mathbf R V_C$, the inverse of $\mathbf L T_C\simeq\mathbf L L_C$, by this specified mate. Both right adjoints are computed on the already fibrant $F$. Consequently the actual $\beta_F$ is a weak equivalence by [lem-coef-model-localization-detects-weak-equivalences]. Since $a$, units and counits are natural transformations before localization, their localized mate retains mapping spaces, composition homotopies and higher naturality. The projective-diagram comparison of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-coherent-diagrams] identifies the strict fibrant diagram $F$ with its ordinary coherent-nerve functor: use the small discrete simplicial category $C$ and its Dwyer--Kan equivalent coherent realization from step 5. Thus the cone-model comparison is the comparison with cocartesian unstraightening in the statement, using [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening].

source.place: Remark 3.2.5.16 and Corollary 3.2.5.20; the right mate and its derived meaning

proof.text: For $u:C'\to C$, identify $N_{C'}^+(Fu)$ with $N(u)^*N_C^+(F)$ on every simplex: the data on each side are the same string $\sigma:[n]\to C'$ and the same components in $F(u\sigma(\max J))$. The equations, operators and marked-edge tests agree, so this is a marked isomorphism, natural in $F$, without fibrancy assumptions. For two functors $u,v$, successive reindexing sends $\sigma$ to $uv\sigma$, exactly as their composite does, and for an identity it changes nothing. By the adjunction of step 2, the left mates of these isomorphisms are $u_!L_{C'}\cong L_CN(u)_!$. The corresponding cone/unstraightening base identities are in [lem-coef-marked-cone-straightening-quillen]. The base-naturality equality for $a$ in [lem-cbc-relative-nerve-cone-left-comparison], under these left identities, gives the equality of the right mates $\beta$ under the right identities: both mates are obtained by composing $a$ with the counit in step 6. The unit and counit triangle identities cancel the two intervening adjunction pairs. Hence the square comparing $\beta_{Fu}$ to $N(u)^*\beta_F$ commutes under the displayed base isomorphisms. The identity and composite assertions follow from the identity and composite equalities for $a$ and for the cone identities. Localization as in [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] preserves these natural transformations and their composition equalities, so their images give the required coherent base compatibility, not just independent equivalences on objects.

Finally take $u:*\to C$ at $c$. Directly from the subset equations, the fibre of $N_C^+(F)$ is $F(c)$: a simplex with constant base string is determined by $t_{[n]}$, and every other $t_J$ is its restriction. The marking is unchanged. Under the point restriction of the cone identities of [lem-coef-marked-cone-straightening-quillen], $\beta_F$ restricts by step 7 to the point mate of $a_*:T_*\to\mathrm{id}$, whose normalization is part of [lem-cbc-relative-nerve-cone-left-comparison]. The canonical equivalence identifying the point unstraightening with $F(c)$ is the inverse of this mate of the cone point comparison; composing it with the fibre of $\beta_F$ is therefore the identity up to the unit/counit homotopies. Thus the comparison has exactly the claimed identity fibre normalization. The cone identities and step 7 carry this normalization simultaneously for all $c$ and base functors. For a strict transformation $F\to G$, the counit naturality square and naturality of $a$ give the naturality square for $\beta$ by the displayed formula in step 6; after localization these squares and their compositions retain their higher data by [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction]. Finally [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] identifies the fibre functors and transport of these fibrations with their classifying diagrams, with its stated coherent base-change compatibility. This supplies all fibre, diagram, and base-change clauses together.
